This project aims to develop a deep learning-based predictive model that leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to analyze genomic sequences and predict potential off-target sites with higher accuracy. Evaluation will be conducted through cross-validation and benchmarking against existing models using metrics such as precision, recall, and F1 score.

Specifically, the weight-normalized structure ensures stable generalization, while the reject option dynamically abstains from high-risk predictions, improving reliability. This approach would be evaluated by measuring the reduction in misclassification rates on out-of-distribution data and the improvement in confidence calibration, using metrics like Brier score and calibration error.

By designing sgRNAs with optimized PAM positioning based on the facilitated diffusion model, we could improve the speed and accuracy of Cas9 target recognition in the plant genome. The efficiency of editing at specific sites would be evaluated by measuring mutation frequency and fragment deletion rates in F. hindsii, comparing results between standard and PAM-optimized sgRNAs.
